title: Standard-Model Proofs for Sponge-Based Authenticated Encryption
summary: TBC-based designs have standard-model proofs under simulatability, whereas sponge-based designs often use idealized assumptions; whether this gap can be bridged remains open.

formal_statement.body: For leakage-resistant authenticated-encryption constructions, TBC-based designs admit standard-model security proofs under the simulatability assumption, while sponge-based designs frequently require idealized assumptions even for black-box security proofs. Determine whether analogous standard-model proofs can be obtained for sponge-based designs under simulatability or a weaker physical assumption.

scope.domain: Leakage-resistant authenticated-encryption constructions in symmetric cryptography, comparing TBC-based and sponge-based designs.
parameters: construction family: TBC-based or sponge-based design
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether analogous standard-model security proofs can be obtained for sponge-based designs under simulatability or a weaker physical assumption.

citations.label: Mode-Level vs. Implementation-Level Physical Security in Symmetric Cryptography: A Practical Guide Through the Leakage-Resistance Jungle

progress.summary: The source contrasts TBC-based constructions, which allow standard-model proofs under simulatability, with sponge-based constructions, for which idealized assumptions are frequently used even in black-box proofs. It presents bridging this gap under simulatability or a weaker physical assumption as an interesting open problem.
citation_labels: Davide Bellizia et al., Mode-Level vs. Implementation-Level Physical Security in Symmetric Cryptography: A Practical Guide Through the Leakage-Resistance Jungle
